title: Not three.
paragraphs:
Not three.
And maybe… not as clean as you think.
Because the real scandal isn’t the number.
It’s who showed up… and who didn’t.
This story might expose something you’ve been hiding.
You’ve seen the scene your whole life.

Three wise men.
Polished.
Peaceful.
Perfectly placed in a quiet nativity.
“Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea… behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem.” (Matthew 2:1)

No number.
No crowns.
No guarantee they were kings.
And here’s the part that should shake you.
Men who read signs in the sky.
Men who, by religious standards, would not pass your holiness checklist.
You can raise your hands in church…
while your heart is chained to something hidden.
That thing you swore you’d stop…
You look fine on the outside.
And the longer you hide it…
the easier it becomes to pretend.
That’s exactly what happened in Jerusalem.
When King Herod asked where the Messiah would be born, the religious leaders answered instantly:
some men from far away, with less knowledge but more hunger…
Because something in them refused to stay comfortable.
Distance from God is not always about ignorance.
Because deep down, you already know.
It’s costing you intimacy with God.
You can live years like this.
but far enough to avoid transformation.
But Jesus didn’t come for half-hearts.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
and the ones no one sees.
Sin is not just what you do.
“Your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God…”
the story doesn’t end in separation.
“When they saw the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy.” (Matthew 2:10)
“Going into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him.” (Matthew 2:11)
Because the Gospel is not about information.
Here’s the truth you need to hear, not avoid:
You cannot clean your own heart.
You cannot earn your way back.
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.” (John 3:16)
Jesus lived the life you failed to live.
Then He died the death you deserved.
“And God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Not after you got your act together.
Victory over the very thing you think still owns you.
You are more broken than you admit.
you are more loved than you ever imagined.
It’s the same as it was then.
But they had one thing many people today don’t:
So here’s the question that matters now:
Will you keep managing your sin…
Because you can sit near truth your whole life…
Don’t let that be your story.
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
if something in you is saying “this is real”—
because you’ll need this reminder when the old patterns try to pull you back.
